definition: A 7B vision-language Qwen model, and across 5 sources the archive's default multimodal training backbone -- chart-reasoning curricula, multimodal verifiable-reward robustness, structured spatial reasoning and general-capability forgetting all use it. Its appearances give the archive most of what it knows about multimodal reinforcement learning: that gains do not survive paraphrase or template change without an invariance constraint, that a binary verifier conflating format with content is the traceable cause, and that splitting perception from reasoning into separately rewarded segments is worth several points over a single outcome signal. It also appears among the models in the pass@k study of whether reinforcement learning expands the reasoning boundary. None of the sources describes its architecture.

evidence.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
evidence.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

evidence.note: Traces the brittleness of multimodal RLVR gains under paraphrase and template change to two properties of the standard objective -- a binary verifier that cannot distinguish a wrong answer from a misformatted one, and a training distribution covering a thin slice of the prompts a deployed model meets -- and fixes both with a trinary reward and an invariance penalty across semantically equivalent prompts.
evidence.title: Improving Generalization Robustness of Multimodal RLVR

evidence.note: Splits a spatial-reasoning chain of thought into explicitly typed segments -- perception, including depth, and reasoning -- and gives each its own process reward and its own advantage term, so that the two do not compete for credit under a single outcome signal.
evidence.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

evidence.note: Confirms that prolonged RLVR makes models forget foundational skills, and counters it with experience replay whose objective weights adapt online to convergence and instability signals.
evidence.title: Beyond Reasoning Gains: Mitigating General-Capability Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
evidence.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

name: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
